items.title: RunBrain Experiment Guardrail — make the advice loop impossible to crash
items.summary: The current RunBrain experiment matcher can reference an undefined `hay` value when a saved safe-opener experiment does not directly name the current loadout, perk, mode, or difficulty. That is exactly the kind of quiet local-first intelligence bug that makes a zero-token coach feel flaky right after it earns the player's trust.
items.recipe: Define a normalized config haystack inside `matchesExperiment()`, add a regression where safe-opener intent has no direct entity match, and keep the matcher zero-network/zero-token.

items.title: Recent-Killer Revenge Drill — turn repeated deaths into a front-door mastery target
items.summary: The game already records recent enemy deaths and widens telegraphs for repeated killers, but the home action stack does not explicitly tell players what to study next. Promoting a clustered killer into a Revenge Drill closes the loop from death memory to menu intent without adding backend cost or balance risk.
items.recipe: Add recent-killer clustering to `buildFrontDoorActionStack()`, insert a `revenge_drill` action when one enemy owns 3+ recent deaths, and test that the drill carries the killer type and Most Wanted study CTA.

items.title: Remembered Controller Glyphs — make device trust visible in onboarding and controls
items.summary: Session 77 taught the game to remember controller profile metadata, but the help surfaces still mostly speak in generic Xbox/PlayStation pairs. A shared label map lets first-run tutorial, Command Center controls, and pause controls show Xbox or PlayStation-specific bindings, including remembered profile fallback before reconnection.
items.recipe: Add `getControllerLabels()` to `src/utils/gamepad.js`, use it in `TutorialOverlay`, `MenuPanels.ControlsPanel`, and `PauseMenu`, pass controller type through `App.jsx`, and use HomeV2's stored controller profile as a controls-panel fallback.
